newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE-Warriors coach quiet on Robson row.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-Warriors coach quiet on Robson row.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Feb 21 - Auckland Warriors rugby league coach John Monie is refusing to speculate on his future if chief executive Ian Robson is axed, NZPA reported on Friday.

Warriors chairman Gerald Ryan and his deputy Brian Blake will meet Robson on Monday to discuss his contract and there is strong speculation that Robson's volatile relationship with his board will come to an end.
Robson is understood to have told people on both sides of the Tasman that he believes his time is up following an informal meeting of the Warriors board this week which he did not attend.
Board members have been tight-lipped about the meeting, fearing they could give Robson grounds for claims of unfair dismissal if he is removed.

Robson and Monie have worked in close harmony, including guiding the club into Super League's ranks, and should Robson go, it could cloud Monie's future, particularly if his side continue to under-achieve.

"I'll have to make a statement if something happens but I'm better off waiting until events unfold," said Monie, who added that he was contracted to Super League, as opposed to the Warriors, for another two years.
"All I will say is that Ian is one of the finest sports administrators I have met and I'm sure he would have no problems getting a job elsewhere.

"It is very difficult to stay focused when these things are going on around you. All I know is that we will be playing Brisbane in front of 50,000 of their fans next week and I've got to concentrate on that."
If the rumours are correct, Robson will become a victim of what some of his board regard as his maverick ways and poor financial performances by the club.

He has been strongly backed by major sponsors Dominion Breweries in the past but they are apparently unhappy that he could not secure an agreement from Super League to have its logo on the playing jerseys.
Changes to the board have put more pressure on him and the recently elected former Kiwis player Dean Lonergan is known to have battled Robson hard around the table.
Robson described Monday's meeting as "business as usual."
Meanwhile, Kiwis and Warriors reserve grade coach Frank Endacott wants answers about his future from his two employers by May.
Endacott said today that he had "no intention of cutting anyone's throat", but he did not intend to remain a reserve grade coach for the rest of his career.
Endacott's contract with the New Zealand Rugby League and the Warriors ends this year and he wants his future sorted out soon.
"We play Australia in the Anzac Day test and I want answers about my future by May 1," he said.
"I would love to stay in Auckland and I love this club but if I've got to move on, I've got to move on.
"A lot will depend on what John (Monie) is doing but I don't want to be a reserve grade coach for ever -- I think I'm better than that."
